front.title: Evidence for AI Inference Execution and Result Binding Using RATS

abstract.t:
AI inference services may execute within Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), confidential virtual machines, protected processes, or heterogeneous platforms containing accelerators. Remote attestation can provide evidence about the identity, integrity, configuration, and operational state of components. Such evidence does not, by itself, establish that a particular inference request was processed by a particular model representation, that the claimed computation was faithfully performed, or that the result delivered to a relying party is the result of that operation.
This document defines an architecture for associating inference-operation evidence, model and runtime identity, execution-assurance evidence, freshness context, and the delivered result. It applies the RATS architecture and existing IETF formats without defining a new RATS role, protocol, cryptographic primitive, EAT claim, or universal inference-result format. It distinguishes integrity of association from evidence of computational execution and from semantic correctness.
